spans.s: [cf. Gk. ζεύγνυμι, ζυγόν; Lat. jungere, jugum; Lith. jùngus; Slav. igo; Goth. juk; Germ. joh, Joch; Angl.Sax. geoc; Eng. yoke.]

2. यु॑ज् mfn. (mostly ifc.; when uncompounded, the strong cases have a nasal, e.g. nom. युङ्, युञ्जौ, युञ्जस्, but अश्व-युक् &c., Pāṇ. vii, 1, 71) joined, yoked, harnessed, drawn by, RV. &c. &c. (cf. अश्व-, हरि-, हयोत्तम-युज्)
furnished or provided or filled with, affected by, possessed of (instr., mostly comp.), MBh.; Kāv. &c.
exciting, an exciter (e.g. युण् भियः, an exc˚ of fear), Bhaṭṭ.
being in couples or pairs, even (not odd or separate), Lāṭy.; Mn.; MBh. &c.
a yoke-fellow, companion, comrade, associate, RV.; AV.; Br.
a sage who devotes his time to abstract contemplation, W.
a pair, couple, the number ‘two’, Pañcar.
homogeneous, similar, equal in rank or power, RV.
union, alliance, relationship, RV. (with जमद्-अग्नेः) N. of a Sāman, ĀrṣBr. (v.l. युग्य).
